scope: Twenty-seven newly verified pre-registered sources from three non-overlapping read-only reviews. No new external sources.

verified_claims: ParseBench evaluates about 2,000 human-verified enterprise pages across tables, charts, content faithfulness, semantic formatting and visual grounding.
Its comparison of 14 methods found no consistently strongest method; the reported 84.9% LlamaParse Agentic result is benchmark-specific.
records.boundary: Corpus, dimensions and scores are benchmark-specific and do not guarantee production parser quality.

verified_claims: The study compares fixed-size, breakpoint-semantic and clustering-semantic chunkers for document retrieval, evidence retrieval and retrieval-based answer generation.
Semantic chunking cost did not produce consistent gains across the evaluated tasks.
records.boundary: Results do not show that semantic chunking is universally unhelpful or that fixed-size chunking is always optimal.

verified_claims: Late chunking embeds long-text tokens first and chunks before mean pooling so chunk vectors retain surrounding context.
The paper reports improved retrieval on its evaluated tasks with long-context embedding models.
records.boundary: Requires compatible long-context models; reported gains are model and task specific.

verified_claims: The study evaluates 36 chunking methods, 6 domains and 5 embedding models.
Content-aware chunking outperformed a naive fixed baseline in the study, while domain and embedding interactions remained substantial; smaller or more numerous chunks increase index and latency cost.
records.boundary: Metrics and winning strategies are limited to the study corpus, models and evaluator; no universal best strategy follows.

verified_claims: Adaptive-RAG routes questions by predicted complexity among no retrieval, single-step retrieval and iterative retrieval.
Its classifier and open-domain QA experiments report efficiency and accuracy improvements over the compared baselines.
records.boundary: Classifier labels, thresholds and gains are specific to the reported datasets and models.

verified_claims: The framework jointly performs intent classification and ambiguity resolution with targeted clarification questions using lightweight open-source LLMs.
It reports turn and conversation metrics and an e-commerce deployment result, including lower reported inference cost and misrouting.
records.boundary: Synthetic-data and one deployment results are not universal or inherently RAG-specific.

verified_claims: SPLADE learns sparse lexical expansion representations with log-saturation weighting and explicit sparsity regularization.
The representation is compatible with inverted indexes and exposes an effectiveness-efficiency trade-off through sparsity.
records.boundary: Reported competitiveness and sparsity behavior are model, training and benchmark specific.

verified_claims: RRF combines rankings using the sum of 1/(k+rank), with k=60 fixed after the paper's pilot.
The reported TREC and LETOR experiments generally outperform the compared individual and fusion systems.
records.boundary: The historical collections and fixed k do not establish universal superiority or an optimal deployment k.

verified_claims: monoT5 generates relevance-label target words from T5 and uses target-token logits as ranking probabilities.
Its MS MARCO, Robust04 and low-data experiments report competitive or improved ranking under the tested settings.
records.boundary: Results are checkpoint, benchmark and training-regime specific and do not describe all rerankers.

verified_claims: RankGPT uses prompted LLM passage permutations, sliding-window reranking and permutation distillation.
The paper reports competitive results on tested IR benchmarks and a distilled 440M student result on BEIR.
records.boundary: Prompt, model, window, distillation and benchmark settings limit the claims; no blanket production superiority or cost guarantee.

verified_claims: RECOMP provides extractive and abstractive compressors that summarize retrieved documents before generation.
Its selective augmentation can return an empty string when documents add no information; compression and quality results are reported for the paper's tasks.
records.boundary: Compression rate and faithfulness are limited to the paper's models, data and training setting.

verified_claims: ALCE evaluates end-to-end retrieval-supported answers with fluency, correctness and citation-quality metrics.
Its ELI5 experiments report that the best tested systems still lacked complete citation support for about half of answers.
records.boundary: The reported rate and metric correlation are specific to ALCE datasets, systems and prompts.

verified_claims: The work distinguishes insufficient context from failure to use sufficient context.
Its selective-generation experiments report a 2-10% increase in correct-answer proportion under the tested models and data.
records.boundary: Model, data, autorater and experimental conditions limit the result; sufficiency is not an absolute automatic fact.

verified_claims: RAGTruth contains about 18,000 natural RAG responses with case-level and word-level human hallucination annotations and intensity.
The paper compares hallucination detection methods and reports competitive small-model detectors after fine-tuning on the corpus.
records.boundary: Corpus, annotation protocol and detector comparisons do not establish production hallucination rates.

verified_claims: RAGAs is a reference-free RAG pipeline evaluation framework covering retrieval context relevance/focus, faithfulness and generation quality.
The paper presents reduced dependence on ground-truth annotation as a framework goal.
records.boundary: Reference-free metrics do not remove the need for domain calibration and human acceptance.

verified_claims: ARES evaluates context relevance, answer faithfulness and answer relevance with a lightweight LM judge trained on synthetic data.
Prediction-powered inference uses a small amount of human annotation in the reported knowledge-intensive tasks.
records.boundary: Accuracy and domain transfer claims are limited to the paper's tasks, synthetic training and PPI setup.

verified_claims: RAGChecker supplies fine-grained diagnostics for retrieval and generation.
Its meta-evaluation reports stronger correlation with human judgments than compared metrics and analyzes eight RAG systems.
records.boundary: Comparative correlation and architecture findings are limited to the evaluated systems and meta-evaluation.

verified_claims: The study identifies position, verbosity, self-enhancement and reasoning biases in LLM-as-a-judge and evaluates mitigation ideas.
GPT-4-level judges exceeded 80% agreement with human preferences in the reported MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena settings.
records.boundary: These are open-ended chat preference evaluations, not direct evidence of RAG factuality or faithfulness.

verified_claims: PoisonedRAG models malicious knowledge injection that targets selected questions in a RAG knowledge base.
Its million-text experiments report about 90% attack success with five injected texts per target question under the stated threat model.
records.boundary: Attack rates and defense results are limited to the paper's attacker, corpus, target and tested defenses.

verified_claims: The attack separates a retrieval trigger fragment from an attack fragment and constructs both using embedding access.
The paper reports near-100% retrieval on its 11 benchmarks and an over-80% GPT-4o SSH-key exfiltration rate in its poisoned-email multi-agent scenario.
records.boundary: These preprint results and rates are restricted to the stated attack algorithm, models, benchmarks and workflow.

verified_claims: The public author report lists legal-text RAG and Agent interview scenarios involving offline/online pipelines, chunking, evaluation, failure attribution, tool fallback, permissions and provenance.
records.boundary: This is personal interview and preparation evidence only; it does not establish company systems, universal parameters or technical authority.

verified_claims: The public exercise repository provides VectorRAG with FAISS, GraphRAG multi-hop components and an optional RAGAS benchmark structure.
records.boundary: Repository exercise structure is not benchmark evidence or proof of production superiority.

verified_claims: The pinned index README organizes public Agent/RAG interview materials, exercises and learning routes and links to external resources.
records.boundary: A secondary index is discovery evidence only; linked originals must support any technical or provenance claim.

verified_claims: The public personal question bank lists RAG fundamentals, pipeline, chunking, embedding, hybrid retrieval, reranking, GraphRAG, evaluation and deployment challenge questions.
records.boundary: It proves public question coverage only; author answers, metrics and recommendations need primary evidence.

verified_claims: The pinned MIT-licensed README presents 100 public RAG questions across ten architecture categories with a cheatsheet and decision tree.
records.boundary: Question-bank categories and counts are repository claims, not company provenance or answer authority.

verified_claims: The author describes a project using OCR and LiteParse-related subprocess ingestion, page provenance, parent-child chunks, timeout handling, temporary-file cleanup and configurable OCR adapters.
records.boundary: This project write-up is scenario evidence; its parameters and product capabilities are not authoritative or universal.

verified_claims: The author retrospective describes a single project evolving from vector retrieval to BM25 plus vector, RRF, reranking and fallback, with query rewrite and candidate-gate discussion.
records.boundary: Reported metrics, parameters and gains are limited to the author's single corpus and explicitly rough implementation.
